title: Ivo and the Horizon
premise: Casper Hartwell, a desert ranger who has spent nine years outrunning the grief of a failed expedition, is hired by his old rival Sera Voss to escort a salvage crew to the drowned city of Qeth-Amar before monsoon season seals the wastes. The job was sworn off after it killed half their company — including Casper's brother — but the map Sera carries is real, and so is the buyer waiting on the other side of the sands. What they find beneath Qeth-Amar is not treasure but a living thing: an engine of the old world that grants power by consuming memory, and Casper watches allies turn on each other as it feeds. In the end, Casper destroys the engine at the cost of his own memories of his brother, chooses love for Sera over the duty that has hollowed him, and leads the survivors home in silence just as the monsoon breaks.
about_author: Zephyrine Dunmore is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent six years mapping arid basins across three continents before turning to fiction. Her novels are known for landscapes that behave like characters and heroes who would rather keep walking than face what they left behind.

chapters.title: The Weight of Stillness
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Tracking a water-thief across the flats, Casper catches him, then lets him go because the man's desperation mirrors his own. A courier delivers Sera Voss's contract: the Qeth-Amar job, sworn off since the disaster that killed his brother Tomas. Emotional beat: restlessness curdling into dread; Casper signs anyway because stopping costs more than moving.

chapters.title: Nine Names on a Door
chapters.summary: POV Casper. He joins the crew in the border town of Halven's Rest and finds Sera older, harder, unapologetic. The roster includes old hands from the first expedition and strangers who don't know its history. They pass the sealed door of the guild hall where the dead are commemorated. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened; rivalry with Sera crackling with unfinished history.

chapters.title: Salt and Second Chances
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Leading the column into the deep waste, Sera reflects on why she took the job — debts, and a buyer who knows too much. A sandstorm forces the crew into a cave where Casper saves a stranger's life using techniques Tomas taught him. Emotional beat: grudging respect between rivals; guilt surfacing like bones in shifting sand.

chapters.title: The City That Drinks Light
chapters.summary: POV Casper. They reach Qeth-Amar at dusk, its towers drinking the last light. Beneath the plaza they find the descent shaft, still warm after centuries. The first night in camp, someone opens a sealed case meant for the return trip. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by violation; Casper realizes the job was never salvage — it was retrieval for someone specific.

chapters.title: What the Engine Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Sera. In the engine chamber, the machine reads touch like text, returning fragments of the holder's past. The navigator Ilex touches it and forgets her daughter's name mid-sentence, gaining instead perfect recall of the route out. Crew members begin volunteering. Emotional beat: seduction of power; Sera feels its pull and lies about what she saw.

chapters.title: A Bargain Struck in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The buyer's agent, embedded in the crew all along, reveals himself and demands the engine's core be cut free. Two crew members side with him; Sera refuses, bound by a promise Casper didn't know she made to Tomas. First blood is spilled. Emotional beat: betrayal; Casper torn between duty to the mission and the growing truth that the mission itself is the corruption.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Storm clouds mass on the horizon as the splinter faction seizes the core and flees down the dry riverbed. Casper and Sera pursue, and in a night camp she finally tells him how Tomas died — not heroically, but reaching for the engine. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into fury; love admitted aloud for the first time, against every rule of duty.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The chase ends at the flooded cisterns where the splinter faction, half-consumed by the core they carry, have forgotten why they're running. Ilex sacrifices herself to collapse the passage, buying time. Emotional beat: sacrifice and horror; power shown devouring those who thought they could hold it.

chapters.title: Everything He Kept
chapters.summary: POV Casper. With the monsoon hours away, Casper enters the chamber alone. To destroy the engine he must feed it everything — and it takes Tomas: his voice, his face, the reason Casper kept moving. He burns the core from inside and walks out unable to say his brother's name. Emotional beat: climax and terrible cost; belonging chosen over the self that duty built.

chapters.title: Rain on the Flats
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The survivors walk out under the first rain in a year, carrying nothing worth selling and a story no one will hear. Sera takes his hand without asking what he lost. In Halven's Rest, Casper adds a tenth name to the guild hall door — his own — and turns toward a life that stops. Emotional beat: resolution; grief without memory, love without duty, and at last, stillness.
